key_insight: Slower cooling shifts an approximately 10 nm AlCoCuFeNi high-entropy alloy nanoparticle from an amorphous toward a crystalline final structure.
engineering_relevance: Cooling-rate control may help tune atomic order in high-entropy alloy nanoparticles during thermal processing.
method: Classical molecular dynamics with an embedded atom model potential.
Potential-energy tracking, adaptive common-neighbor analysis, and radial distribution functions.
evidence_signal: Simulations showed cooling-rate-dependent final structures and pronounced temperature hysteresis between melting and crystallization.
watch_item: Results concern an approximately 10 nm simulated particle at extremely rapid cooling rates; transfer to experiments or larger particles requires validation.
paper_title: AlCoCuFeNi High-Entropy Alloy Nanoparticle Melting and Solidification: A Classical Molecular Dynamics Simulation Study
